item.text:
Implemented the pure-`std` Rust port in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml), [test4.rs](/output/test4.rs), [src/lib.rs](/output/src/lib.rs), [src/idna.rs](/output/src/idna.rs), and [src/idna/predicates.rs](/output/src/idna/predicates.rs). The CLI matches the C++ program: it reads only the first positional argument from `std::env::args()`, defaults to `example.com`, ignores extra args, and prints the same four `0`/`1` lines.

Black-box probing of `/workspace/dataset/test4_executable` showed the matching behavior is based on UTF-8 byte length and ASCII detection: `is_valid_domain` is `!empty && len <= 255`, `is_valid_label` is `!empty && len <= 63`, `is_ascii_domain` is `input.is_ascii()`, and `is_idn_domain` is `!empty && !input.is_ascii()`.

Both builds succeeded: `cargo build --release` and `rustc --edition=2021 test4.rs -o test4`. I verified byte-for-byte output parity against the C++ binary on default invocation, empty input, malformed ASCII cases, Unicode cases, and the 63/255-byte boundary cases.
